result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You were in hospital with a chest infection (community-acquired pneumonia). It was in the lower part of your right lung (right lower lobe).
Your CURB-65 score is 1.
In hospital you had antibiotics into a vein (IV) for 1 day. Then you had amoxicillin tablets.
You may feel tired for several weeks. Your cough may last 3 to 6 weeks.

## What you need to do
1. Take your amoxicillin tablets for 3 more days. This makes 5 days of antibiotics in total.
2. Have a repeat chest X-ray (CXR) in 6 weeks at the Radiology Department. It checks that the infection has cleared.

You do not need to book the chest X-ray. A request has been sent.

## Dates and medicines
- 5 October 2026: you were admitted to hospital.
- 7 October 2026: you left hospital.
- 10 October 2026: last dose of amoxicillin.
- In 6 weeks: repeat chest X-ray at the Radiology Department. No exact date is given.

Medicine:
- Amoxicillin, 500 milligrams, three times a day (TDS). You had 2 days of antibiotics in hospital. Take tablets for 3 more days.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What day will my chest X-ray be?
- How will I get the result of my X-ray?
- What does my CURB-65 score of 1 mean for me?

## When to get urgent help
See your GP or call 111 if:
- you become more short of breath
- your fever comes back
- you cough up blood

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.
